caption:
Google Cloud shipped Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.1: curated agent context as portable markdown and YAML bundles, not another proprietary catalog API.

The thesis is direct: your model is rarely the bottleneck. Missing or fragmented context is. Table definitions, metric math, and runbooks still sit across wikis, drives, and engineers' heads.

OKF formalizes the LLM-wiki pattern Karpathy outlined. One concept per file, path as identity, markdown links as the graph, and only type required in frontmatter. That is closer to metadata-as-code than to dumping embeddings and hoping retrieval guesses right.

Defender move this week: if your team exports runbooks or data docs for agents, pin the bundle in git, PR-review edits, and limit which tools can write back into the bundle.

narration.text: Your agent probably does not need a bigger model. It needs curated context in a shape any tool can read.
Google's Open Knowledge Format v0.1 packages that context as markdown files with YAML frontmatter in a portable bundle.
That beats hoping retrieval stitches siloed catalogs and wikis together at query time without mistakes.
Treat those bundles like infrastructure. Version them, PR-review edits, and control which agents can write back.
Would you review an agent wiki like a Terraform module? Tell me in the comments.
